section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch13 — Types of Validity (Complete)
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: Researchers designing a new 'creativity test' check whether scores align with the theoretical characteristics creativity is expected to have. This process of checking whether a test truly measures its underlying theoretical concept is called establishing:
explanation: Construct validity concerns whether a test genuinely measures the theoretical construct it claims to, distinct from content validity (domain coverage).

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch13 — Types of Validity (Complete)
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: An entrance exam's scores are checked against students' actual academic performance two years later, to see if high scorers indeed go on to perform well. This is an example of establishing:
explanation: Predictive validity correlates test scores with a FUTURE outcome/criterion. Concurrent validity instead correlates with a criterion measured at the SAME time.

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch13 — Types of Validity (Complete)
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A parent looks at a maths test paper and remarks, 'this certainly looks like a proper maths test' — based purely on its superficial appearance, without any statistical analysis. This is the weakest, most subjective form of validity, called:
explanation: Face validity is merely whether a test APPEARS to measure what it claims — a subjective, non-statistical judgment, the weakest form of validity evidence.
